title: Joining Stan Getz with Jimmy Cobb; Getz fires a pianist for applause
summary: Sam and Jimmy Cobb join Getz, who is deep in drugs; in St. Louis he fires pianist John after a big ovation.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: And everybody started going a different way. I went--I went to Stan Getz. And that was another experience. Me and Jimmy Cobb went to Stan Getz.
Uh huh.
And we stayed there. I stayed there for about a year.
What was that all--what was that like?
Quite an experience, I can tell you very
*Nat Adderley joined J.J. Johnson's sextet, 1957-58; then Woody Herman's orchestra in early 1959.
much. It was quite an experience because at that time, Stan Getz was--was uh, deep into--in drugs at that time.
Uh huh.

You see. I remember an incident, man, there was a John Hicks--no, not John Hicks, John--what that boy's name--piano player--excellent piano player from Philadelphia, man. He lived in California--that John--what's his name--this guy can play, man, play piano. But Stan Getz, he ah, he couldn't stand nobody getting no bigger applause than he--
Oh yeah.
That's funny. And that's funny to say, but that's--
That was a strange dude.

Yeah, that was the case. Well, we was in St. Louis at the Glass Bar. And uh, and we're staying in the hotel. All we got to do is come downstairs, downstairs in the basement to the nightclub and play, man.
Uh huh.
Catch the elevator. But he--he would always be late. And so at this one particular night, the club owner would ask us to please--cause the, the, the nightclub was jam full of people.
Uh huh.
And uh, and uh, Stan Getz, for some reason, he drew more women than he drew men, you know.
Uh huh.
Lot of women was weird but a lot of women came to, to, to, to hear the band.
Uh huh.
You know. Well he's the--had the little baby boyish look, you know. And the women loved it.
Yeah.

And he played--he could play a ballad, you know, he could really swoon on them ballads. So we started playing, man, so--and he came down there and he said "who told ya'll to start playing?" So we told him, say "the club owner asked us to start playing." "Well who's paying you--the club owner or me?" So everybody say well, wait a minute, now we don't want to get involved in this stuff, you know, to who's paying who, you know what I mean. Said that--so everybody clammed up. And he said "well, look. Let me tell you something. If I don't show, I don't--I don't want nobody to play. I don't care what nobody's saying. If I don't show, you won't play." So we said "fine. That's fine with me." So anyway, the gig went on. So we started playing. So after we got through playing a song, John was playing a solo. And he played, man. The people was moving along with the music.
Uh huh.
And after he played his solo, man, the people just said "Raaah." A long ovation of applause.
Uh huh.

So he looked at John and said, 'you know that's going to cost you your gig, don't you?' So everybody laughed, you know. We thought he was kidding. He wasn't. After we finished that night, paid John off.
What?
That's right. Paid him off and gave him his ticket back. 'No one get applause more than I do.'
He's a corny dude, though.
